name: TShark & Wireshark — Switches, Panes, Capture & Display Filters
description: TShark is the CLI version of Wireshark — same capture engine, no GUI. Both use BPF for capture filters (same syntax as tcpdump) and Wireshark's proprietary display filter syntax for post-capture analysis. Wireshark GUI has three panes: Packet List (orange), Packet Details (blue), Packet Bytes (green). Display filters are more powerful than capture filters — applied without losing packets.
source: CDSA Module 07: Intro to Network Traffic Analysis
notes:
=== TSHARK SWITCHES ===
-D                  List available network interfaces
-i eth0             Select capture interface
-f 'host x.x.x.x'  Capture filter (BPF syntax, same as tcpdump)
-c 100              Stop after capturing 100 packets
-a duration:60      Auto-stop after 60 seconds
-r file.pcap        Read from PCAP file
-W <format>         Set output format (e.g., pcapng)
-P                  Print packet summary (even when writing to file)
-x                  Print hex dump of packet data

=== TSHARK COMMON USAGE ===
# Live capture to file
tshark -i eth0 -w /tmp/capture.pcap

# Live capture with BPF capture filter
tshark -i eth0 -f 'port not 22' -w /tmp/capture.pcap

# Read PCAP with display filter (Wireshark syntax)
tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'http.request.method == GET'

# Print verbose packet details
tshark -r capture.pcap -V

# List interfaces
tshark -D

# Auto-stop conditions
tshark -i eth0 -a duration:60 -a filesize:1000 -w /tmp/cap.pcap

=== TSHARK DISPLAY FILTER EXAMPLES ===
tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'ip.addr == <IP>'
tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'tcp.port == 443'
tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'http'
tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'dns'
tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'ftp'
tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'ftp-data'
tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'frame.number == 4'

=== WIRESHARK GUI PANES ===
[ORANGE] Packet List Pane
  → Shows all captured packets as rows
  → Columns: No. | Time | Source | Destination | Protocol | Length | Info
  → Click a row to select it — highlights corresponding bytes in green pane
  → Right-click: Follow Stream, Apply as Filter, Export, Mark/Ignore

[BLUE] Packet Details Pane
  → Protocol tree for selected packet
  → Expand layer: Frame → Ethernet → IP → TCP → Application
  → Right-click a field: Apply as Filter / Prepare as Filter / Copy
  → Shows all header fields, flags, options

[GREEN] Packet Bytes Pane
  → Raw hex + ASCII of selected packet
  → Highlighted bytes correspond to selected field in blue pane
  → Useful for spotting encoded data, patterns in payloads

=== WIRESHARK CAPTURE FILTERS (BPF — applied BEFORE capture) ===
# Same syntax as tcpdump — applied before packets arrive in Wireshark
# Set in: Capture → Options → Capture filter field
# Downside: packets NOT matching are lost permanently

host <IP>              → traffic to/from host
net <NETWORK>/<CIDR>   → traffic to/from subnet
port 80                → TCP/UDP port 80
not arp and not icmp   → exclude noise
tcp and port 443       → HTTPS only
src host <IP>          → from source only

=== WIRESHARK DISPLAY FILTERS (proprietary — applied AFTER capture) ===
# Applied to already-captured packets — can change without losing data
# Enter in the filter bar at top of Wireshark
# Green bar = valid filter, Red bar = invalid syntax

ip.addr == <IP>          → packets involving this IP
ip.src == <IP>           → source IP only
ip.dst == <IP>           → destination IP only
tcp.port == 443          → TCP port 443
udp.port == 53           → UDP DNS
http                     → HTTP traffic
dns                      → DNS queries + responses
ftp                      → FTP control channel
ftp-data                 → FTP data transfer
icmp                     → ICMP only
not arp                  → exclude ARP
http.request.method == "GET"  → HTTP GET requests only
frame.number == 4        → specific packet by number
tcp.stream eq 1          → all packets in TCP stream 1

=== LOGICAL OPERATORS IN DISPLAY FILTERS ===
# AND / OR / NOT + parentheses for grouping
ip.addr == <IP1> && tcp.port == 80       → AND
ip.addr == <IP1> || ip.addr == <IP2>     → OR
!(arp || icmp)                           → NOT (exclude both)
